summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and chronic depression was admitted for severe hyperglycemia (glucose 802) and abdominal pain with hematochezia. She was diagnosed with hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state and treated with IV fluids and an insulin drip, later transitioning to subcutaneous insulin. Her abdominal pain was chronic and possibly exacerbated by metabolic derangements, with hematochezia attributed to hemorrhoids. CT imaging showed stable cirrhosis and no acute intra-abdominal pathology. She improved with treatment, her kidney function normalized, and she was discharged home on a new insulin regimen with close follow-up. A severe headache on discharge day prompted a head CT, which was normal. She remains committed to sobriety despite psychosocial stressors.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperosmolarity without nonketotic hyperglycemic-hyperosmolar coma (NKHHC)
